span.label: **PRIMING AS THE CONFOUND RATHER THAN THE PHENOMENON, WHICH THIS CORPUS HAS ALMOST NONE OF:** `Quotation withheld.` Two accounts of one effect, and **the priming account needs no control process at all** - if the current trial repeats the previous trial's stimulus and response, the pairing was already formed. So a CSE is not evidence for cognitive control until the overlap is removed. Every other record I have tagged treats priming as the object of study; here it is the alternative explanation
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **AND THE AUTHORS SAY PLAINLY THAT THE EARLIER WORK - INCLUDING THEIR OWN - LEAVES THE QUESTION OPEN:** `Quotation withheld.` The preceding sentence - that earlier tasks did not control for those confounds - is fused in the staged text and cannot be quoted. **This is a whole literature's results placed in doubt by the people who produced some of them**, and it is what motivates the design rather than a limitation conceded at the end
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **THE DISSOCIATION IS PRODUCED BY A CONTROL RATHER THAN BY A MANIPULATION, WHICH IS THE RARER AND STRONGER FORM:** initiation times showed the effect `on BOTH confound-minimized and confound-laden trials`; reach curvatures showed it `on confound-laden BUT NOT on confound-minimized trials`. **Nothing was added to the design - something was taken away, and one of the two measures lost its effect with it.** A dissociation obtained by subtraction cannot be explained by whatever the added factor also did, which is the usual objection to the added-manipulation kind
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **AND THE STROOP TASK APPEARS HERE AS APPARATUS, NOT AS SUBJECT:** a three-response, reach-tracking version, 84 years after Stroop 1935, used to ask about trial-to-trial control rather than about interference. **The corpus now holds the founding paper and a paper that treats it as equipment** - and the pair is worth more than either, because it shows what happens to a paradigm when it stops being a finding and becomes a method
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

'Scherbaum, Dshemuchadse, Fischer, and Goschke (2010, Exp. 2) OBSERVED A SIGNIFICANT CSE in participants' hand movements in a mouse-tracking version of the Simon task, Quotation withheld, whereas th[is study]...' The disagreement is between two analyses of the same confound, not between two claims about the effect. Q-444.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: associative priming —causes→ CSE
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.7 — **ONE OF TWO RIVAL ACCOUNTS, AND `has been attributed to` IS THE HEDGE, INSIDE THE QUOTE.** This edge is not the paper's finding - it is the position the paper tests. Weight 0.7 because the sentence reports an attribution in the literature rather than a result here, and because this paper's own data cut both ways: the curvature CSE disappears when the priming confound is removed (so priming was carrying it) while the initiation-time CSE does not (so priming was not). **A corpus that recorded only the surviving effect would lose the reason anyone doubted it.**
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: conflict adaptation —causes→ CSE
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.7 — THE OTHER RIVAL, on the same sentence and at the same weight, deliberately. The two edges are symmetrical because the quote is symmetrical - it lists both without choosing. **Recording one and not the other would make the corpus take a side the sentence does not take**, and the paper's contribution is precisely that it separates them empirically rather than arguing for one. The separation lives in the third sense.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: associative priming —contrasted-with→ conflict adaptation
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — **THIS IS THE EDGE THE PAPER IS ABOUT**, and it is the only one of the three that carries the paper's own claim rather than the literature's. The two accounts predict the same effect and differ in whether a control process is needed at all - one is top-down regulation, the other is feature repetition requiring nothing. Weight 0.9: the contrast is explicit in the quote and the whole design exists to resolve it.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Initiation times showed main effects of both current and previous congruency whether or not associative-priming confounds were present, supporting a threshold adjustment process that is not reducible to priming.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Reach curvature showed a congruency sequence effect only on confound-laden set repeat trials and not on confound-minimized trials, indicating that the curvature CSE is driven by associative priming rather than conflict adaptation.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The size of the curvature CSE was itself reliably larger on set repeat than on confound-minimized trials.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: On confound-minimized trials reach curvature responded only to current congruency, with no carry-over from the previous trial and no interaction.
